## Design

### 2026-10-17 – so this was me trying to go off on my own after reading the tutorial. i spent this whole hour just trying to figure out how to make this cool helix path! i learned:

**1.1h**

so this was me trying to go off on my own after reading the tutorial. i spent this whole hour just trying to figure out how to make this cool helix path! i learned:

- plane -> circle -> cylinder -> helix
- then make the face of the sweep from the helix
- don't forget the new button when using extrude. i was so confused why it was adding to a new part...

things I'll have to learn later:

- how to connect this path to the pole at the top

i'm already deviating from my initial design. i decided to move the staircase to the middle, after the ball has begun moving.

### 2026-10-18 – this time i made the staircase - and it was easier than i thought it would be! although i still made a lot of mistakes, and parts of my staircase are very imprecise. i messed up often when using the c

**1.32h**

this time i made the staircase - and it was easier than i thought it would be! although i still made a lot of mistakes, and parts of my staircase are very imprecise. i messed up often when using the copy and paste tool.
this time, i spent way too long trying to figure out how to make an angled plane when you need a line to make a plane and a plane to make a line when i realized i can make planes based off the edges of my parts! paradox solved.

this time i tried to connect the helix path to the post with a sweeped path in the middle. and it was soo hard trying to connect them correctly. when i first made the helix path, connecting it to the post was definitely something i should have considered. but anyways, since i couldn't get it perfect, i just made it so that the sweeped path is above the helix and the ball can fall into the helix. its a good thing gravity is here to help.

### 2026-10-18 – i worked on the plinko track.

**1.85h**

i worked on the plinko track.

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 180322](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/OOCRjeIOZQfDKMp1Kj2CfqBggVc5VwbS/2029e7796a7bbc07979a80ea8b28860ef6757dbcdd62ad14ada4550072333b07.png)

it took a lot of effort, especially since i was imprecise in some parts. i had to redo  one whole line of the pins inside because i was afraid they were too close to the edge and would disrupt the ball's movement. learned a lot though:
- don't forget to double check the direction you are extruding
- order you're extruding matters. first the connect the whole thing, and then the parts on top, otherwise youll get a "boolean resulted in ... " error
- tidy up the sketch before trimming to make parts easier to select when extruding
- use the constraint tool to close shapes properly... it took a while to fix the shapes because they looked closed, but when i zoomed in they weren't!

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/1061d647-dd66-4c56-9333-7be93d3b0295/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-18 – this time, i added the finishing touches! i connected the plinko track to a path to lead to the base, and also created a boundary to collect the ball. neither was that hard. for a while, i was worried

**0.87h**

this time, i added the finishing touches! i connected the plinko track to a path to lead to the base, and also created a boundary to collect the ball. neither was that hard. for a while, i was worried because of how the paths had extended past the base, but i was able to resolve this thanks to the transform tool.

the real issue this session was the staircase. i already had a feeling that it was not wide enough for my marble, but i really amateurly ignored it. this time i measured it, so i had to trouble shoot that. i couldn't fix my extrudes because this would mess up all the other parts below the staircase.
- maybe in the future, i should figure out how to build the parts separately
i was finally able to fix this by using the scale transform tool, and picking a point very close to the staircase to minimize its displacement! i owe the transform tool this project.
